AbstractText.Label: AIMS
AbstractText.content: A new L-asparaginase produced by Streptomyces ansochromogenes UFPEDA 3420 actinobacteria was used in this study against human lymphocyte cultures to evaluate the immunological profile induced by this enzyme.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS AND RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Cultures of lymphocytes were stimulated with S. ansochromogenes L-asparaginase and cytotoxicity, cell viability, cell stimulation and cytokine production were analyzed. This new S. ansochromogenes L-asparaginase induced activation and proliferation of the TCD8+ lymphocyte subset and produced higher TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-2 and IL-10 levels in a 24 hour assay.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: S. ansochromogenes L-asparaginase is a promising molecule to be used in in vivo models and to deepen pre-clinical tests against Acute Lymphoblast Leukemia.

AbstractText.Label: SIGNIFICANCE AND IMPACT OF STUDY
AbstractText.content: L-asparaginase is an indispensable component of the chemotherapeutic treatment of Acute Lymphoblast Leukemia (ALL) and Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). Currently, drugs as Asparaginase® , Kidrolase® and Elspar® and Erwinase® are efficient against leukemic disease, but promote immunosuppression and other side effects in human organism. Our purified S. ansochromogenes L-asparaginase showed promissory results inducing, in vitro, higher immunostimulation in human PBMC, especially in T CD8+ lymphocytes subsets.
